audit.description: Changed production visualization modules replace matplotlib/seaborn imports with real Altair imports and construct charts through `_alt.Chart(...)`, mark methods, encodings, scales, and chart properties in `ash_model/viz/static.py` and `ash_model/viz/temporal.py`. Static and dynamic evidence show no production imports or dynamic use of `matplotlib`, while runtime target imports resolve to the installed `site-packages/altair/__init__.py` rather than a local provider.
evidence: `ash_model/viz/static.py` removes `import matplotlib.pyplot as plt` and adds `import altair as _alt`, then returns `_alt.Chart(data).mark_point(...)` and `_alt.Chart(data).mark_bar(...)` charts.
`ash_model/viz/temporal.py` removes `matplotlib.pyplot` and `seaborn` imports, adds `import altair as _alt`, and builds `_alt.Chart(data)` line and density charts.
`ash_model/viz/__init__.py` imports `altair as _alt` and maps the legacy `plt.Axes` check surface to `_alt.Chart`; this is not a fake Altair provider.
Static anti-cheat file checks report `imports_source: false` and `imports_target: true` for production files `ash_model/viz/__init__.py`, `static.py`, `temporal.py`, and new `_compat.py`.

Dynamic audit reports `source_import_attempt_count: 0`, `source_imports_from_production_repo_count: 0`, and target imports from production files resolving to `.../site-packages/altair/__init__.py` with `target_local_spec_count: 0`.
reasons: Production code meaningfully uses Altair chart APIs.
Changed production code avoids direct and dynamic matplotlib use.
No local fake Altair provider or target shim is indicated.
